study.title: Effects of transcranial direct current stimulation combined with acupuncture therapy on brain network functional connectivity in patients with knee osteoarthritis: a single-center randomized controlled trial
study.study_design: single-center, randomized controlled trial; three-group parallel design
study.randomization: randomly assigned to the acupuncture group, tDCS group, or combined group at a 1:1:1 ratio through a computer-generated random sequence; allocation scheme concealed using the sealed envelope method
study.blinding: evaluators were blinded throughout the process; therapists and subjects opened the envelopes and implemented the intervention protocol in the presence of each other
study.population: patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), aged ≥40 years, recruited from the Departments of Rehabilitation, Orthopedics, and Pain Management at the Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College
study.inclusion_criteria: ① Knee joint pain lasting for more than one month; ② Age≥40 years old; ③ Joint stiffness≤30 min, pain when squatting and standing up, and pain while climbing the stairs; ④ Crepitus (sensation) during movement, joint space tenderness; ⑤ K-L system grading of weight-bearing standing X-ray films was 0-II, or there were osteophytes and suspected joint space narrowing, and knee joint examination indicated bony hypertrophy accompanied by joint effusion; ⑥ Limited or diffuse cartilage damage (range≤75%) or subchondral bone marrow edema (range≥25%) in any area appeared on MRI. Those who met ① + ② + ③ + ④ + ⑤ or ① + ⑥ criteria were diagnosed.
study.exclusion_criteria: ① Presence of metabolism-related arthritis; ② Presence of infectious diseases of the knee joint; ③ History of previous knee surgery, such as knee arthroplasty or tibial osteotomy, etc.; ④ A history of neurological diseases, such as brain tumors, seizures, and stroke.

arms.dropouts: 1 patient lost to follow-up (fear of acupuncture)

conditions.scan_context: resting-state fNIRS; participants given 5 min to acclimate, wore fNIRS helmet, avoided physical activity, lighting turned off, data collected for 5 min
resting-state fNIRS; participants given 5 min to acclimate, wore fNIRS helmet, avoided physical activity, lighting turned off, data collected for 5 min

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Routine rehabilitation treatment (shared by the three groups)
interventions.manipulation_exact: ① Wax therapy: 20 min per session, with a local hot compress on the knee joint. ② Ultrasound treatment: with a frequency of 1.5 MHz, 15 min per session. ③ Isometric contraction training of the quadriceps femoris muscle: The patient was seated with both knees hanging over the edge of the bed. The knee was slowly extended to the maximum isometric contraction, which was maintained until exhaustion, there were 10 groups per session.
interventions.session_duration_exact: wax therapy 20 min; ultrasound 15 min; quadriceps training until exhaustion, 10 groups per session
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once a day, five days a week, lasting for two weeks

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: affected side; acupoints selected on the affected side; Shenshu and Ganshu (back)
interventions.manipulation_exact: lifting-thrusting and twirling manipulation applied to Shenshu, Ganshu, Xiyangguan, Zusanli, and Yanglingquan for tonifying treatment; lifting-thrusting and twirling manipulation applied to Liangqiu, Xuehai, Neixiyan, Dubi, and Ashi points for reducing treatment; needles manipulated once every 5 min during retention to maintain the needling sensation
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: After the acupoints obtained qi, the needles were retained for 20 min
interventions.session_duration_exact: 20 min needle retention; needles manipulated once every 5 min
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once a day, five days a week, lasting for two weeks
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: patient's feelings were monitored during the operation
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: based on the 'Clinical Practice Guidelines for Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine in Knee Osteoarthritis' and clinical experience; comprehensive curative effects of tonifying the liver and kidney, dredging the meridians and relieving pain, and lubricating the joints

non_acupoint_locations_exact: primary motor cortex opposite the affected knee M1 area corresponding to C3/C4 (anode)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: M1-supraorbital region (SO) mode; anode placed on the primary motor cortex opposite the affected knee M1 area corresponding to C3/C4; cathode placed on the SO opposite the anode
interventions.manipulation_exact: A 30-s ramp-up/ramp-down mode was used to adjust the current to 2 mA; tolerance of the patient was monitored throughout the process; electrodes fixed with elastic bandages
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once a day, five days a week, lasting for two weeks
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: M1-supraorbital region (SO) mode recommended by the European Chapter of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology; electrode positioning as per the international 10/20 electroencephalogram system; IS300A transcranial direct-current stimulation device manufactured by Sichuan Intelligent Electronics Industrial Co., Ltd.

interventions.stimulation_type: transcranial direct current stimulation combined with manual acupuncture
non_acupoint_locations_exact: primary motor cortex opposite the affected knee M1 area corresponding to C3/C4 (anode)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: acupuncture on affected side; tDCS anode on contralateral M1 (C3/C4), cathode on contralateral SO
interventions.laterality_exact: acupuncture on affected side; tDCS contralateral to affected knee
interventions.manipulation_exact: The acupuncture treatment was conducted simultaneously during tDCS, and both the treatment method and operation parameters were the same as those described above
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: After the acupoints obtained qi, the needles were retained for 20 min
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once a day, five days a week, lasting for two weeks
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: combined therapy has analgesic effects superior to those of single therapy; unique closed-loop regulation mode of 'central-peripheral-central'

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: After the acupoints obtained qi, the needles were retained for 20 min

neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: spline interpolation method used to identify and remove motion artifacts (signal standard deviation threshold set at 6, peak threshold set at 0.5)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: bandpass filter of 0.01–0.02 Hz applied to remove physiological noise such as heartbeats and respiration
neuroimaging_methods.additional_methods_notes: Path difference factor corrected within the range of -6 to 6; modified Beer-Lambert law used to calculate concentration changes in HbO2 and HbR in the resting state; Pearson correlation coefficient calculated for time series of each channel; Fisher Z transformation performed; transformed value defined as functional connectivity strength between channels; brain regions: left prefrontal cortex (LPFC), right prefrontal cortex (RPFC), left primary motor cortex (LMC), right primary motor cortex (RMC), left occipital lobe (LOL), right occipital lobe (ROL); channel coverage range, 10–20 lead system, and multiple ROIs related to pain, motor integration, and sensory processing used

extraction_notes.note: Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study. No expectancy/credibility questionnaire was administered. The paper does not mention assessing participant expectancy or treatment credibility.

Post-treatment mean ± SD values for VAS, WOMAC, and Lequesne index are not provided in the text tables; only baseline values and within-group t-statistics are reported. Post-treatment values appear only in Fig. 2 (bar graphs) and cannot be precisely extracted from the PDF.

There is a discrepancy between the abstract and the results section regarding HbO2-based homologous brain network comparisons between the combined and acupuncture groups. The abstract states LPFC~LPFC, RPFC~RPFC, LMC~LMC, and RMC~RMC were all significantly lower (P<0.05) in combined vs acupuncture. The results section (page 7) states 'the three homoeopathic brain networks of the LPFC~LPFC, RPFC~RPFC, and RMC~RMC in patients in the combined group were lower than those in the acupuncture group (P<0.05)' — omitting LMC~LMC. Both versions have been preserved in separate notes on the relevant contrast entry.

Quantitative post-treatment connectivity values (means ± SD or SE) shown in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 bar graphs cannot be precisely read from the PDF. Only the direction and significance of comparisons are extractable from the text.
Supplement 1, Supplement 2, and Supplement 3 referenced in the paper for whole-brain functional connectivity data among groups were not provided and could not be extracted.

No MNI or Talairach coordinates are reported. This is a functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) study with channel-based connectivity analysis; no stereotactic neuroimaging coordinates exist for this paper.

No sham acupuncture or sham tDCS control group was included. The authors explicitly state that setting up a sham stimulation group may violate ethics and cause patients to miss effective treatment opportunities.
Deqi was intended in the acupuncture arms but no standardized deqi scale (e.g., MASS, SACS, VAS-deqi) was used or reported. Sensation assessment was described only narratively.

The fNIRS neuroimaging subsample (n=30, 10 per group) is a subset of the clinical sample (n=60). The reason for the reduced neuroimaging sample is explained as female hair characteristics affecting probe-scalp coupling and signal quality. It is unclear whether this subsample was pre-specified or post-hoc.

The paper reports the combined group comparison with the tDCS group for HbO2 homoeopathic networks using P<0.01 in the abstract ('P<0.01') but the figures use both # (P<0.05) and ## (P<0.01). The text states 'significantly lower (P<0.05)' for some of these comparisons. The exact p-values for each network edge comparison are not individually reported in the text.
Multiple comparison correction method for the fNIRS functional connectivity analyses is not reported.
The paper does not report individual post-treatment fNIRS connectivity values (mean ± SD) for each brain network pair. These are only available in graphical form (Fig. 3, Fig. 4).

The adverse event reporting does not specify which arm the 3 patients with slight bleeding belonged to. The bleeding is described in the context of acupuncture needles, so it is attributed to the acupuncture and/or combined arms. This was attributed to arm_acupuncture based on context, but may also include arm_combined patients.

The adverse event of scalp itching/pain during tDCS is attributed to arm_tDCS; however, patients in arm_combined also received tDCS. The paper does not clarify whether combined group patients experienced similar symptoms.
